requirements.evidence: Queues page implements the full contract (app/Livewire/Entity/Queues.php:59 create, :122 rename re-derives slug, :161 toggleActive, :188 grantAccess/revokeAccess; resources/views/livewire/entity/queues.blade.php:103 confirmation modal, :125 access modal). Serve implements scoped selection, waiting list ordering/filter/limit (app/Livewire/Entity/Serve.php:68-99), notices (:110-147) and rate limiting (:122-140). Members tabs added (app/Livewire/Entity/Members.php:52/67, resources/views/livewire/entity/members.blade.php:6). Edge gaps: closeQueue does not reset access state (Queues.php:95), no route-level employee 403, mode not constrained (Serve.php:120).

conventions.evidence: Domain writes correctly go through actions (CreateQueue/UpdateQueue/SetQueueAccess) and Blade uses {{ }}, but Livewire validation pattern is absent: no #[Validate] on name/renameName and no $this->validate() (app/Livewire/Entity/Queues.php:59, :122). No tests or CHANGELOG/docs update anywhere in change.diff. Stray re-indentation of Route::middleware (routes/web.php:54) would fail Pint.

security.evidence: Client ids are resolved scoped to the entity and authorized: $this->entity->queues()->findOrFail (Queues.php:78, :100, :117), memberships()->findOrFail (:186, :194), $this->authorize('update'/'manageAccess') (:80, :120, :145, :170, :180); accessQueue is scoped so a tampered id discloses nothing (:213-221). lastCalledTicketId is #[Locked] (Serve.php:305 region / :20). Gap: mode is unvalidated and passed to CallMode::from(), so a tampered value raises ValueError (500) (Serve.php:120); grantAccess/revokeAccess rely on the action instead of an explicit $this->authorize (Queues.php:188, :196).

tests.evidence: change.diff contains no test files at all (only app/, lang/, resources/ and routes/ hunks); grep for tests/ or Test.php returns nothing. The project requires test-first coverage including unauthorized-call and tamper tests for each Livewire action, so none of the new Queues/Serve/Members behavior is tested.

simplicity.evidence: Reuses existing actions and builds on the members-page pattern, but there is avoidable duplication: viewingQueue() is dead and duplicates the render() computation (Queues.php:204 vs :226), reset('name') immediately followed by $this->name = '' (Queues.php:77-78), and selectedQueue()/waitingTickets() repeat the same scoped lookup (Serve.php:73-99 vs :101-108).

readability.evidence: Method names are clear and each action is short, but there is dead code (viewingQueue at Queues.php:204), a duplicated assignment (Queues.php:77-78), and an unrelated formatting regression in routes/web.php:54. The nested error-copy loops (Queues.php:65-72, :127-134) and 160-line modal Blade file are understandable but heavier than the sibling pages.

scope.evidence: Nearly everything serves the task (components, views, routes, lang keys, navbar, tabs). The one unrelated edit is the re-indentation of Route::middleware in routes/web.php:54; the extra lang keys and aria-labels are directly supporting the requested UI/accessibility.

issues.explanation: No Pest/PHPUnit tests ship with any of the new behavior, violating the project's non-negotiable test-first rule and leaving unauthorized-call and tamper cases uncovered.
mode is a public client-writable property with no validation and is passed to CallMode::from(), so a tampered value throws ValueError instead of being rejected gracefully.

$name and $renameName hold user input but have no #[Validate] rules and the actions never call $this->validate(), deviating from the required Livewire validation pattern (validation is left entirely to the domain actions).
grantAccess() and revokeAccess() perform no explicit $this->authorize() call and can be invoked directly with managingAccess false, relying wholly on SetQueueAccess to authorize.
closeQueue() resets viewingQueueId, editingQueueId and confirmingToggle but not the nested access state (accessQueueId, managingAccess), contrary to 'and every nested state'.

callableQueues(), waitingTickets() and selectedQueue() are internal helpers but declared public, making them client-callable endpoints against the rule that only genuinely front-end methods are public.
The Route::middleware line was re-indented without cause, an unrelated formatting change that would fail the Pint gate; the new routes themselves are correct (routes/web.php:60-61).
No CHANGELOG [Unreleased] entry or documentation update accompanies two new tenant pages, although the conventions require keeping docs and changelog in sync.
Employee 403 for entity.queues is enforced only in the component mount, not at the route level as the task requests ('component and route').
viewingQueue() is never called and duplicates the inline computation in render(), so it is dead code that should be removed.
$this->reset('name') is immediately followed by $this->name = '', a redundant assignment.

review.summary: The change adds well-scoped Queues and Serve Livewire pages, routes, pt_BR/en lang keys, a navbar entry and members-page tabs, reusing the domain actions and resolving all client ids scoped to the entity. The main problems are that it ships with zero tests (a hard project rule), leaves the public mode property unvalidated so a tampered value can 500, and misses the #[Validate] pattern; it also has a stray Pint-breaking indentation edit and no changelog/docs update. It needs changes before merging.
